key_terms.meaning: A thread is an execution path inside a process; threads in one process share the same address space.
A race condition occurs when the result depends on the unsynchronized timing of accesses to shared data.
A mutex is a lock that lets one thread at a time enter a critical section.
An OpenMP parallel region is a block marked with #pragma omp parallel that a team of threads executes.
A reduction clause gives each thread a private partial value and combines them with an operator at the end.
An MPI rank is the integer identifier of a process inside a communicator.
An MPI communicator is a group of processes plus a context that keeps their messages separate.
A collective is an MPI operation, such as broadcast or reduce, in which all ranks in a communicator take part.
SIMT means single instruction, multiple threads: one instruction controls many GPU threads that may branch separately.
A warp is a group of GPU threads scheduled together; NVIDIA warps contain 32 threads.
A CUDA kernel is a device function launched by the host to run as many threads on the GPU.
A CUDA grid is the collection of all thread blocks launched by one kernel.
A CUDA thread block is a group of threads that can share block-level memory and synchronize.
In CUDA, shared memory is fast on-chip storage visible to all threads in one block.
Global memory is device DRAM visible to all threads in a grid and to the host through transfers.
Constant memory is read-only device memory cached for broadcast to many threads.
A coalesced access has adjacent threads read or write adjacent memory addresses in one transaction.
A host-device transfer copies data between CPU memory and GPU memory, usually with cudaMemcpy.
An NDRange is the OpenCL index space of work-items launched by a kernel.
A work-group is a set of OpenCL work-items that share local memory and barriers.

takeaways: Threads share memory, so OpenMP is easy to add but shared updates still need synchronization.
MPI processes do not share memory; every cooperation is an explicit send or receive.
A GPU executes many threads in warps, so branching and memory access patterns decide speed.
A CUDA kernel launch fixes grid and block dimensions, and those dimensions map each thread to data.
Shared memory is per block and fast; global memory is large but slow; constant memory is read-only and cached.
Host-device copies are often the largest cost, so move data once and reuse it on the device.
Coalesced, reused data turns GPU bandwidth into useful work.
OpenCL expresses the same device ideas with NDRanges, work-groups and local memory.
Choose OpenMP for one node, MPI across nodes, and GPUs for regular data-parallel work.
bank_note: Long answers usually ask you to connect a programming model to its memory model, show correct synchronization or indexing, and justify performance choices with transfer and locality costs.

bank.q: Explain the shared-memory programming model and show how an OpenMP parallel region with a work-sharing loop and a reduction handles a shared sum. Mention what can go wrong without the reduction.
outline: one address space shared by all threads
team of threads created by a parallel region
work-sharing divides loop iterations
reduction gives private partial values and combines them safely
without reduction or atomic update, a race condition can lose updates
Pthreads would need an explicit mutex around the update

bank.q: Describe the MPI programming model: rank, communicator, point-to-point send and receive, and one collective operation. Explain why processes cannot simply read each other's variables.
outline: each MPI process has its own memory
rank identifies a process inside a communicator
communicator gives a group and a message context
send and receive must match source, tag and communicator
collective involves all ranks, for example broadcast or reduce
cooperation is explicit because there is no shared address space
mention deadlock risk from unmatched receives

bank.q: Explain SIMT execution on a GPU. Include warps, thread blocks and why divergent branches reduce efficiency.
outline: one instruction controls many threads
warp is the scheduling group, 32 threads in NVIDIA GPUs
thread block contains several warps and can share block memory
divergent branches make a warp execute paths one after another
memory latency is hidden by switching warps
occupancy depends on resources per block

bank.q: Explain the structure of a CUDA program. Show the kernel launch syntax and how grid, block and thread indices map threads to data.
outline: host code runs on CPU, kernel runs on GPU
kernel declared with __global__ and launched with <<<grid, block>>>
threadIdx, blockIdx, blockDim and gridDim define position
global index combines block and thread indices
host allocates and copies data to device
kernel launch is asynchronous with respect to host code

bank.q: Write an OpenMP program fragment that computes the sum of an array of n integers in parallel. Explain how the reduction avoids a race condition and why a shared variable without protection fails.
outline: use #pragma omp parallel for reduction(+:sum)
loop variable is private by default in work-sharing
reduction creates private partial sums and combines them
unprotected shared sum has a read-modify-write race
mention schedule and load balance
check correctness with small n

bank.q: Write an MPI program outline in which each rank computes a partial sum and rank 0 prints the total. Use MPI_Reduce and state the role of each argument.
outline: MPI_Init and MPI_Comm_rank and MPI_Comm_size
each rank computes a local partial sum
MPI_Reduce with send buffer, receive buffer, count, datatype, MPI_SUM, root and communicator
only rank 0 receives the final total
rank 0 prints the result
MPI_Finalize ends MPI

bank.q: Design a CUDA tiled matrix multiplication kernel. Explain grid and block mapping, shared-memory tiling, __syncthreads, and coalesced global loads.
outline: 2D grid and 2D block map one thread to one output element
load tiles of A and B into shared memory
__syncthreads after loading and before reuse
loop over tiles and accumulate partial products
global loads should be coalesced
watch shared-memory bank conflicts
host-device transfer cost matters at the edges

bank.q: A vector addition kernel runs slowly. Explain how you would check and improve host-device transfers, global memory coalescing and launch configuration.
outline: copy input vectors to device once and output back once
index as blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x
adjacent threads should access adjacent elements
choose block size as a multiple of warp size
enough blocks to fill the device
consider asynchronous copies or streams
measure transfer time separately from kernel time

bank.q: Map an OpenCL vector addition onto host and device code: NDRange, work-group size, kernel arguments and local memory use. Explain how work-item IDs map to array elements.
outline: host creates buffers and kernel
global size equals number of elements
local size defines work-group size
kernel uses get_global_id to index arrays
work-groups share local memory only if needed
vector addition needs no local staging
enqueue kernel and read output buffer

bank.q: Compare OpenMP and MPI for a large scientific simulation. Discuss memory model, synchronization cost, scalability and when a hybrid MPI+OpenMP program is appropriate.
outline: OpenMP uses shared memory threads inside one node
MPI uses processes with separate memories across nodes
OpenMP synchronization is often cheaper inside a node
MPI message passing has network and packing costs
MPI scales beyond one node
hybrid uses MPI across nodes and OpenMP inside each node
load balance and communication volume decide success

bank.q: Analyze why a CUDA kernel with perfect arithmetic can still be slow. Cover memory hierarchy, bank conflicts, coalescing, occupancy and host-device transfer cost.
outline: global memory latency dominates without reuse
uncoalesced accesses waste memory transactions
shared-memory bank conflicts serialize access
low occupancy hides less latency
divergent branches waste warp lanes
host-device transfer can dominate total time
optimization must target the real bottleneck

bank.q: Evaluate the claim: 'Moving a computation to the GPU always makes it faster.' Use transfer cost, parallelism size and data reuse in your answer.
outline: GPU needs enough parallel work
host-device copies add fixed and bandwidth costs
small problems lose to transfer overhead
data reuse on device can amortize copies
coalescing and occupancy affect achieved speed
streams can overlap copy and compute
counterexamples exist for branchy or tiny workloads

bank.q: Design a hybrid MPI+OpenMP+CUDA solution for training a machine-learning model on a cluster of GPU nodes. Justify the division of work and the memory choices.
outline: MPI distributes work across nodes and synchronizes gradients
OpenMP manages CPU-side threads and data preparation inside a node
CUDA kernels handle dense matrix and tensor operations on each GPU
batch data is copied to global memory once and reused
shared memory tiling helps matrix kernels
collectives such as all-reduce combine model updates
memory choices follow scope: registers and shared for fast reuse, global for large tensors
load balance and overlap of copy and compute decide scaling

glossary.def: A thread is an execution path inside a process that shares the process address space with other threads.
Shared memory is a programming model in which threads of one process read and write the same variables.
Distributed memory is a model in which each process has its own address space and cannot directly read another process's variables.
Message passing is cooperation by explicit send and receive operations between processes.
A race condition is a timing-dependent error caused by unsynchronized access to shared data.
Mutual exclusion ensures that only one thread at a time executes a critical section.
A barrier is a synchronization point where threads wait until all members of a group arrive.
OpenMP is a compiler-directive API for shared-memory parallel programming with threads.
Pthreads is a POSIX thread library for creating and synchronizing threads in one process.
MPI is a standard message-passing interface for programs running as multiple processes.
A communicator is an MPI group of processes plus a context for their messages.
A rank is the integer identifier of a process inside an MPI communicator.
A collective operation is an MPI call in which all ranks of a communicator participate.
A GPU is a many-core processor designed to run thousands of threads for data-parallel work.
SIMT is a GPU execution model where one instruction is issued for many threads at once.
A warp is a group of GPU threads scheduled and executed together, 32 threads in NVIDIA GPUs.
A kernel is a function written for device execution and launched over many GPU threads.
A grid is the complete set of thread blocks created by one kernel launch.
A thread block is a group of GPU threads that can share block-level memory and synchronize.
Global memory is large device memory accessible by all threads in a grid and by host transfers.
CUDA shared memory is fast on-chip memory private to one thread block.
Constant memory is read-only device memory that is cached and useful for values read by many threads.
Local memory is per-thread device memory used when registers are insufficient or indexing is dynamic.
Coalesced access is a memory pattern where adjacent threads access adjacent addresses in one transaction.
An NDRange is the OpenCL index space that defines the global and local dimensions of work-items.
A work-group is a set of OpenCL work-items that can share local memory and synchronize.
